# Run KServe images on FIPS-enabled clusters with validated crypto modules

## Description

The KServe components of the model serving stack currently link non-validated
cryptographic libraries in several images. This epic audits the KServe images
for non-validated crypto usage, remediates every finding in the request path
using validated crypto modules, and verifies the remediated images run
correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters. It also produces the KServe
inputs (module inventory entries, build attestations, FIPS-mode test results)
that the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package is assembled from.

## Scope

- Audit every KServe component image: enumerate the linked cryptographic
  libraries and classify each as validated or non-validated, producing the
  KServe portion of the module inventory.
- Remediate all non-validated crypto usage in the KServe request path (image
  base layers, language-runtime crypto, vendored or bundled libraries) so the
  request path uses validated crypto modules only.
- Verify the remediated images run correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift
  cluster, end to end (component deployment, model serving, inference request
  path).
- Verify no regression on standard (non-FIPS) clusters.
- Produce build attestations and FIPS-mode test results for the remediated
  images and hand them to the compliance evidence effort.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the KServe component images, when they are audited against the
  validated-crypto module classification, every non-validated crypto library
  linked in the request path is identified (measured by: the module inventory
  covers every KServe image with each crypto module classified, and no
  unclassified entry remains).
- Given the remediated KServe images deployed on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift
  cluster, when the serving stack is exercised, all components run correctly
  using validated crypto modules (measured by: end-to-end serving tests pass
  on a FIPS-enabled cluster with no non-validated crypto in the request path).
- Given the remediated images deployed on a standard cluster, when the
  existing KServe test suite runs, no regression is introduced (measured by:
  the existing test suite passes).
- Given a remediated image build, when the build completes, build attestations
  and FIPS-mode test results are produced and available to the compliance
  evidence package effort (measured by: attestations and test results exist
  for every remediated KServe image).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0) — covers the KServe portion of "all serving-stack images run
  correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no
  non-validated crypto in the request path)".
- HLR-2 (P0, enabling) — produces the KServe module-inventory entries, build
  attestations, and test results that the compliance evidence package is
  assembled from.

# Gate KServe builds against FIPS crypto regressions

## Description

Adds a gating CI check to the KServe build pipeline that fails any KServe
build which reintroduces non-validated crypto usage, enforcing the
FIPS-compliant state established by the image remediation. This protects the
compliance posture over time: a regression to non-validated crypto in the
serving stack cannot merge unnoticed.

## Scope

- Implement a check that inspects KServe build output and images for
  non-validated crypto usage, classifying crypto modules against the same
  validated/non-validated module standard the image audits are measured
  against.
- Wire the check into the KServe build pipeline as a required part of the
  build result: a build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage fails.
- Make the check actionable for developers: a failure identifies the offending
  crypto usage and how to remediate it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a KServe build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage, when the
  pipeline runs the check, the build fails (measured by: an intentionally
  non-compliant build is rejected by the pipeline).
- Given a build of the remediated KServe images, when the pipeline runs the
  check, the build passes (measured by: the check is green on compliant
  builds).
- Given the KServe build pipeline, when a change is proposed, the check is a
  required part of the build outcome (measured by: the build result reflects
  the check outcome and cannot bypass it as an advisory-only job).
- Given the check's classification, when it is compared with the image audit's
  classification, both use the same validated/non-validated module standard
  (measured by: no divergence between what the audit flags and what the check
  flags for the same image).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1) — covers the KServe portion of "CI enforces FIPS regressions: a
  gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated
  crypto usage".

# Assemble the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package

## Description

Assembles the compliance evidence package for the model serving stack — the
module inventory, build attestations, and test results required for FIPS 140-3
certification — by consolidating the deliverables produced when the
serving-stack images were remediated. The package is the engineering-complete
input to the security review board submission: complete, internally consistent,
and organized per the board's milestone requirements. This epic covers the
assembly of the package; its submission through the security review board to
the external certification lab is out of this epic's scope.

## Scope

- Consolidate the module inventory across all serving-stack images (the KServe
  and Platform Operator portions), covering every image with validated /
  non-validated classification of its crypto modules.
- Collect build attestations for every serving-stack image from the component
  build pipelines.
- Collect FIPS-mode test results (FIPS-enabled cluster runs) for every
  serving-stack image.
- Cross-check the package so each image is covered by all three evidence types
  with consistent image identity and build provenance.
- Organize the package per the security review board's stated milestone
  requirements so it can be submitted without structural rework.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the remediated serving-stack images, when the package is assembled, it
  contains a complete module inventory (measured by: every serving-stack
  image's crypto modules are classified; no image is missing from the
  inventory).
- Given the package, when completeness is checked, every serving-stack image
  has build attestations and FIPS-mode test results attached (measured by: a
  completeness pass over the package finds no missing evidence item).
- Given the package, when consistency is checked, inventory entries,
  attestations, and test results agree on image identity and build provenance
  (measured by: no mismatches across evidence items for the same image).
- Given the board's milestone requirements, when the package layout is
  reviewed, it is organized to match them (measured by: the package is
  accepted as review input at the first board milestone without structural
  rework).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0) — covers the "compliance evidence package (module inventory,
  build attestations, test results) is assembled" portion of the requirement.

# Submit the evidence package through the security review board to the certification lab

## Description

Submits the assembled FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package through the
mandatory security review board sign-offs at the defined milestones to the
external accredited certification laboratory, and drives the submission
through the lab's process. This epic is dominated by human and third-party
process gates rather than engineering work: review-board sign-off at defined
milestones and lab scheduling are externally controlled and cannot be
compressed by engineering effort (the lab's historical turnaround is six to
nine months). The engineering effort involved is coordination and
record-keeping; the duration is dominated by external cadence.

## Scope

- Present the assembled evidence package at the security review board's
  defined milestones and obtain the mandatory sign-offs.
- Submit the package to the external accredited certification laboratory.
- Track board and lab feedback (findings, requests for information) and drive
  each to resolution.
- Record the submission state (milestones passed, submission status) so the
  FIPS support posture can be documented accurately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the assembled evidence package, when the security review board
  milestones are reached, the mandatory sign-offs are obtained and recorded
  (measured by: a sign-off record exists for every defined milestone).
- Given board sign-off, when the package is submitted, the external accredited
  laboratory accepts it for evaluation (measured by: lab acceptance or
  engagement confirmation).
- Given board or lab feedback during the process, when a finding or
  information request arrives, it is tracked and addressed (measured by: no
  unaddressed finding when the next milestone is reached).
- The epic completes when the package is submitted through the board to the
  lab (measured by: submission record exists). The lab's certification
  decision and its timing are outside this epic's control and are not
  completion criteria.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0) — covers the "submitted through the security review board to the
  external certification lab" portion of the requirement.

## Risks and External Constraints

- Lab turnaround is historically six to nine months, and the review board's
  cadence is externally controlled (strategy problem statement and
  open-questions note). Schedule risk is dominated by these third parties; the
  engineering work of the strategy is deliberately not blocked behind this
  epic (tiered delivery).
- The certification decision itself belongs to the lab; the strategy requires
  submission, not adjudication.
